citations.narrative:
The facility conducted regulated activity without a valid USDA license. It canceled its Class B dealer license in February
2024 and transferred three juvenile Canadian lynxes to two facilities in June 2026. The facility representative stated that
he received compensation for the lynxes and sent them for breeding stock. He did not inquire whether the recipient
facilities intended to use the animals for regulated activity, despite both facilities holding USDA Class C exhibitor licenses.
Conducting regulated activity without a USDA license violates the Animal Welfare Act and prevents APHIS officials from
assessing the animals’ care. The facility must obtain a USDA license before conducting regulated activity. Continuing to
conduct regulated activity without an active license is a serious violation of the Animal Welfare Act.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
